_comment: W Linux bar config. USER-OWNED — w-style/w-theme never touch it. Edit and the running bar live-reloads (FileView watch). Any color is a THEME TOKEN name (e.g. surface/inputBg/text/accent/accentFg/border) OR a literal #RRGGBB hex; the matching *Opacity (0.0–1.0) is always separate, so the bar follows theme switches while opacity is tuned per element (set 0 for a fully transparent element, e.g. no button border). Hand-editing is expected and safe. Note that `w-bar` and `w-appearance bar-position` patch this file in place through jq, which rewrites it: keys, order and these comments all survive, but blank separator lines between them do not.
_comment_chrome: The bar's own plaque (bgColor/bgOpacity) and outline (borderColor/borderOpacity) — everything else here paints the blocks ON it. These two opacities are THEME-FOLLOWING by default: unlike the per-element ones they also accept an EFFECTS TOKEN name — "bar"/"barBorder" (the bar's own chrome pair) or "surface"/"scrim" (the shared shell scale) — resolved live from the active theme's effects.conf (W_FX_BAR_OPACITY / W_FX_BAR_BORDER_OPACITY), so a theme can make the bar a solid plaque or dissolve it entirely. Writing a number here pins it and the bar stops following the theme; delete the key or write the token back to hand it over. Dropping both to 0 (in the theme, or here) leaves the blocks floating as separate islands — their zone backgrounds are their own. Outline WIDTH is geometry, not this (W_GEO_BAR_BORDER, default 0).
_comment_geometry: GEOMETRY IS THEME-OWNED and deliberately absent below. position/height/radius/margin/padding/gap/borderWidth/minSquare for the bar, and zoneRadius/zonePadding/zoneBorderWidth/buttonRadius/buttonGap/buttonBorderWidth/itemsGap inside blocks, all come from the active theme's geometry.conf (W_GEO_BAR_*, rendered into core/geometry.json by `w-style apply geometry`) — so switching themes reshapes the bar without touching this file. Writing any of those keys back in overrides just that one element and it stops following the theme; delete the key to hand it back. An override is a number (px), or a geometry TOKEN name resolved live ("barRadiusZone", "barGap", "radiusSm", …). Radii additionally accept "pill" = half the element's height (even rounding) and 0 = sharp corners. "minSquare" (true/false, root-level) is the one boolean override: when true, every block's (and every folded `zone`'s) minimum width is clamped to its height with content centered, so small pill/circle buttons stay round instead of oval; content wider than the height still grows the block as before.
_comment_enabled: Every block takes an optional "enabled": true|false at its root (default true). "enabled": false drops the block entirely — it is never instantiated and none of its background work (Process / FileView / UPower-Pipewire subscriptions) runs. This is the GLOBAL composition switch; per-monitor visibility is the "monitors" map below, which overrides it — so a block shipped off here is switched back on for one screen from W Hub -> Appearance -> Bar, without editing this file. Four blocks ship OFF on purpose: systemMonitors (the cpu/ram/temp/disk group), network, brightness and kbdBacklight — they are at-a-glance readouts rather than everyday controls, and each is one click away in the Hub.
_comment_id: Every block also takes an "id": a name unique across the WHOLE file (nested zone items included). It is the handle the per-monitor "monitors" map and the W Hub (Appearance -> Bar) address the block by — "type" cannot serve as one because several blocks may share a type (this file ships two "button" blocks). A block with no "id" still renders normally; it just cannot be addressed per-monitor and is not listed in the Hub. The Hub shows an id's human name from core/i18n.json — "bar.block.<id>" first, then "bar.type.<type>", then the block's own "label", then the bare type — so a hand-added block of a known type is named for free.
_comment_network: Light read-only network indicator — connection-type glyph + primary IP. All management is delegated to nm-applet in the tray (left-click its icon); this block's left-click opens nm-connection-editor (GUI editor). Source: `ip -j route get 1.1.1.1` -> { dev, prefsrc } for the default-route interface (so 'wired AND Wi-Fi both up' shows the winning link; a VPN shows via its tun*/wg* device). Type is classified by device prefix (en/eth -> ethernet, wl -> wifi, tun/tap/wg/ppp -> vpn). No connectivity -> 'disconnected' state (does NOT auto-hide). Liveness: a Timer poll every `interval` ms plus `nmcli monitor` for an instant re-poll on any NM event. Built-in glyphs: ethernet \uf0200, wifi \uf1eb, vpn \uf0582, disconnected \uf0c9d. Settings: showIcon, icon (state object), showText, display ip|ifname, offlineText ("" = glyph only when offline), interval, fontSize, textColor/textOpacity, iconColor/iconOpacity, zone*.
_comment_icon: Blocks with a left glyph expose it as "icon" (toggle the whole icon with showIcon). "icon" is either a single Nerd Font glyph string, or — for multi-glyph blocks — an object of named states: volume → { normal, muted }; battery → { levels: [full, three-quarter, half, quarter, empty], charging }; network → { ethernet, wifi, vpn, disconnected }. An empty string "" (or a missing key) means 'use the block's built-in default glyph' (to HIDE an icon use showIcon:false, not an empty glyph), so the defaults below are blank and documented here. Put a real glyph between the quotes to override. Editor tip: a bare Nerd Font PUA char can get lost on save in some editors — a JSON \uXXXX escape (e.g. "\uf538") is equivalent and safe. Built-in defaults (Nerd Font): clock \uf017, volume normal \uf028 / muted \uf026, battery levels \uf240 \uf241 \uf242 \uf243 \uf244 + charging \uf0e7, brightness \uf185, kbdBacklight \uf030c, cpu \uf4bc, ram \uf538, temp \uf2c9, disk \uf0a0, keyboardLayout \uf11c.
_comment_monitors: System-monitor blocks cpu/ram/temp/disk are lightweight indicators (poll on "interval" ms; click opens btop). Shared opts: showIcon, icon, fontSize, interval, textColor/textOpacity, iconColor/iconOpacity, zone*, and a threshold that paints text+glyph in highColor/highOpacity once the value hits highThreshold. Per-block: cpu → showPercent ("%" load from /proc/stat). ram → display percent|used|usedTotal (used = MemTotal−MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo). temp → lm_sensors `sensors -j`; unit C|F, showDegree, sensorChip/sensorLabel override the auto-detected CPU sensor ("" = auto), auto-hides when no sensor is found. disk → path (mountpoint), display percent|used|free|usedTotal from `df`. Sensible default intervals: cpu/ram/temp 2000, disk 30000. The numeric value uses tabular figures and reserves the width of its widest reading, so changing digits never shift neighboring blocks.
_comment_updates: Block type "updates" is a read-only pending-updates indicator. It does NOT poll pacman itself — the `w-update-check` systemd user timer runs `w-update check` (non-root: checkupdates for repo + `yay -Qua` for AUR, never `pacman -Sy`) and writes ~/.local/state/w/updates.json, which this block watches. count = repo (+ AUR if includeAur). It auto-hides when count is 0 (hideWhenZero, default true) UNLESS a reboot is pending. highColor/highOpacity paint the glyph+count when a reboot is owed — detected reliably by the running kernel's modules dir /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r) being gone after an in-place kernel upgrade. Multi-glyph icon: { available, reboot } (built-in defaults: available \uf06b5, reboot \uf0709). Left-click runs the interactive upgrade (ghostty -e w-update); right-click shows Arch news. Change the check period with `w-update interval <minutes>`. Settings: showIcon, icon (state object), showCount, includeAur, hideWhenZero, interval (status-file reload fallback, ms), fontSize, textColor/textOpacity, iconColor/iconOpacity, highColor/highOpacity, zone*, plus the shared click-flash/cursor keys.
_comment_notifications: Block type "notifications" is the Do Not Disturb indicator + toggle. State comes from ~/.local/state/w/notifications.json (written by `w-notify`), so the glyph flips whichever surface changed it — this block, the Hub panel, a hotkey or the AI. It stays visible by default even when DND is off (hideWhenIdle: true collapses it to 'only while silenced') because a silent desktop with no visible cause is how notifications get missed for days; while DND is on the glyph+label switch to highColor. Multi-glyph icon: { idle, dnd } (built-in defaults: idle \uf09a1, dnd \uf09a2). showText shows the DND deadline (HH:mm) or 'On'. Left-click toggles DND (`w-notify dnd toggle`), right-click opens Hub → Notifications, where the history lives. Settings: showIcon, icon (state object), showText, hideWhenIdle, fontSize, textColor/textOpacity, iconColor/iconOpacity, highColor/highOpacity, zone*, plus the shared click-flash/cursor keys.
_comment_interaction: Every block exposes optional click-flash + cursor controls on its interactive element (the zone for single-unit blocks like clock/volume/cpu/...; each button for multi-button blocks workspaces/apps/tray). They apply wherever present: clickColorLeft / clickColorRight — flash color on LMB / RMB (theme TOKEN name or #RRGGBB); a button with no color set does NOT flash (opt-in per button). clickOpacity — apex alpha 0..1 (default 0.5). clickDuration — full pulse fade-in -> apex -> fade-out, ms (default 300). cursor — hover cursor on that element: pointer | default/arrow | text | crosshair | wait | busy | grab | grabbing | none; omitted = the block's own default (pointer for interactive blocks/buttons, arrow for clock/battery/brightness/kbdBacklight). Setting clickColorRight also makes the element accept RMB (for the flash) on blocks that otherwise ignore it.
_comment_button: Block type "button" is a generic launcher: a clickable pill that runs a shell command on left-click (commandLeft) and, optionally, a different one on right-click (commandRight) — run detached via `sh -c`, so any command works (an empty string is a no-op). Reach the shell's own popups through their Hyprland globals, e.g. hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.global("quickshell:launcher")'. Optional label ("" = none) and optional icon ("" = none): a Nerd Font glyph, a theme-icon name, a /path/to.(png|svg), or the special keyword "w-logo" = the active theme's brand SVG (theme-aware + live). Image icons get iconMode tint|solid|original + iconStrength/iconShade/iconLift (like apps/tray); a glyph is colored by iconColor. gap = space between icon and label (drops out when either is absent). Settings: icon, label, gap, iconSize, fontSize, commandLeft, commandRight, iconMode/iconStrength/iconShade/iconLift, textColor/textOpacity, iconColor/iconOpacity, zoneColor/zoneOpacity/zoneBorderColor/zoneBorderOpacity, plus the shared click-flash/cursor keys.
_comment_zone: Block type "zone" is a decorative wrapper that groups other blocks behind one shared background, and can fold. Its nested blocks live in a top-level "items": [ ... ] (sibling of "settings", each item a normal block honoring "enabled"). settings: zoneColor/zoneOpacity (shape comes from the theme) + optional "folded": { enabled, trigger: "hover"|"click", chevron: bool, icon (Nerd Font glyph OR theme-icon name OR /path/to.png — image icons get iconMode tint|solid|original + iconStrength/iconShade/iconLift), iconSize, iconColor, iconOpacity, iconGap, label, fontSize, textColor, textOpacity }. Folded shows just icon+label; hover reveals the blocks (icon+label crossfade out, items slide+fade in), click keeps icon+label as a persistent toggle handle. folded.enabled=false ⇒ always-expanded decorative meta-block.
_comment_multimonitor: Optional per-monitor map: output name -> { enabled, show, blocks }. ALL THREE ARE OPTIONAL and each answers a different question. "enabled" — is there a bar on this output at all: an explicit true/false always wins (so the PRIMARY monitor's bar can be switched off here too); with the key absent the primary monitor (set by `w-monitor primary`, W Hub -> Displays) gets a bar and any other output gets one only if it has an entry here at all. "show" — a sparse { "<block id>": true|false } map overriding, for THIS output only, whether each block is shown; an id missing from it falls back to that block's global "enabled". This is what W Hub -> Appearance -> Bar writes, and it is kept when the bar is switched off, so switching it back on restores the same composition. "blocks" — the heavy hammer: a full { start, center, end } replacement of the block composition for this output (same { type, id, settings } shape as the root "blocks"), for a deliberately different bar on a second screen; settings are then a separate copy that no longer follows the root. Geometry/colors are never per-monitor (that would desync popup baselines). Example: { "HDMI-A-1": { "enabled": true, "show": { "tray": false, "systemMonitors": false } } }.
